figures.caption: The default packet returns twelve consumed bytes, an aliased payload pointer and four decoded fields.
figures.alt: Five annotated details at parser return. Hexadecimal and native signed-decimal views show status twelve and payload address input plus eight. Input begins at 0x10010004 with the twelve valid packet bytes after its guard. Record A at 0x10010108 contains flags one, sequence 4660, payload length three and payload-sum residue 254. Caller status/pointer stores have not executed.

figures.caption: Eleven available bytes exclude the checksum trailer even though it remains mapped and visible.
figures.alt: Five annotated details at parser return for an eleven-byte prefix of the unchanged valid packet. The available register is eleven; native signed status is minus one and the payload pointer is zero. The mapped checksum byte 0x1a is visible at input plus eleven, just beyond the logical prefix. All four record A words retain minus one.

figures.caption: A checksum failure returns minus six and makes no output-record stores.
figures.alt: Five annotated details after validating a complete packet with a corrupted checksum. Available count is twelve. Only the final trailer changes from 0x1a to 0x1b. Native signed status is minus six and the payload pointer is zero. The four record A words retain their initial minus-one values; execution tracing establishes no stores to the record.
